data.about: A single node where three bars meet, loaded along one of them. The force polygon of the node is built by drawing parallels to the bars: a closed polygon means the node is in equilibrium, and the sense of each force tells whether its bar is in compression (blue) or tension (red).

steps.caption: step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: place the node where the three bars meet
steps.title: Node A

steps.caption: dashed circle of radius R around A: the bar ends lie on it
steps.title: Guide circle

steps.caption: choose B on the circle and draw bar 3 = A–B
steps.title: Bar 3

steps.caption: left: F pulls on the node along bar 3 — right: from pole F4, the same vector, F × scale → G
steps.title: The load — in both diagrams

steps.caption: left: choose C, bar 1 = C–A — right: dashed parallel to bar 1 through one end of the load vector
steps.title: Bar 1 — form and parallel

steps.caption: left: choose D, bar 2 = D–A — right: dashed parallel to bar 2 through the other end
steps.title: Bar 2 — form and parallel

steps.caption: the two parallels intersect at H: the polygon closes
steps.title: Point H

steps.caption: G–H is the force in bar 2, H–F4 in bar 1 — the bars flash on the left
steps.title: Forces in bars 1 and 2

steps.caption: closed polygon = equilibrium; blue = compression, pink = tension
steps.title: Compression / tension
